An after-set with zero failures admits no added failure whatever the baseline held, so added_failure_count is 0 and added_failure_ids is empty; this review's own head re-run (logs/review-gate-head.log) also finishes 105 passed, EXIT=0, so the zero is measured at the committed revision as well as reported by the worker.

findings.summary: The fix carries the placement reason out of _owner_ready so the row records it, but the failover bound is still decided before the closure ever runs: max_wait is computed from `routing == 'pinned'` at router.py:2444 while routing is still None (no owner was resolved), and the closure only sets routing inside gate.acquire at router.py:2422 via ready=_owner_ready. So the request that waits for its engine to appear and is then found to be pinned to it waits the gate's full default 300 s instead of the 30 s bound the pin exists to give it, and the timed-out/failover branch at router.py:2459 cannot fire because max_wait is None. This is the second half of the prior review's finding at the same path; the row's value is repaired, the wait policy is not.

The handoff loop adds the wait at the engine-less owner-wait gate (`_owner_wait_gate`, router.py:2014, 'a gate that belongs to no engine') into `waited`, and router.py:2509 then labels the whole gate_wait_s with the engine whose gate finally admitted the request. A reader summing queue cost per engine (the attribution the fix's own comment at router.py:2506-2508 states) therefore charges discovery time spent at no engine to the engine the request was bound to, which is the same misattribution shape the failover sum was added to remove. No row is wrong by more than the owner-wait interval, so it does not hold the node.
